jobs.title: Sourcing Specialist, Supply Chain
jobs.description_text: Tecovas was founded with the simple goal of making the world's best western boots, apparel and leather goods - and selling them at a fair price. We are a brand revolutionizing a category and welcoming first-time boot buyers and western enthusiasts alike. Tecovas is looking for a Sourcing Specialist, Supply Chain to support the growth and expansion of our supply chain across footwear, apparel, and accessories. Reporting directly to the Sr. Category Manager, you will own purchase order placement and critical sourcing data, monitor production timelines, support vendor management, and help improve the processes and tools that keep product moving from concept to customer. This role is required to be based in Austin, TX. Candidates must either be currently located in or willing to relocate to Austin, TX. What you’ll do: Own purchase order writing and maintenance across footwear, apparel, and accessories, ensuring accurate and timely placement and updates. With many of our own products functioning as critical components to our own and our customers’ missions, the Supply Chain team has a direct impact on the success of our rocket and satellite programs. They set up the assembly kits that enables our technicians to put together our Electron rockets, manage inventory, look after shipping and receiving, manage direct and indirect procurement, and inspect and ensure that all of our materials and products are compliant and up to standard. They are the chain that links our teams together, and are critical to our success. PRODUCTION PLANNER I Based onsite at Rocket Lab’s headquarters in Long Beach, CA, Production Planners are responsible for work order management at Rocket Lab. Production Planners interact with Engineering, Quality, Production, Supply Chain, and Finance, to ensure they are planning and managing the production schedule, production lead times, yield management, and engineering build timelines. Production Planners ensure that the Production team has work in their queue, the correct priority, and are clear to build without blockers. WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO: Responsible for supply and fulfilment planning within MRP for Production work orders. jobs.description_text: SPACE SYSTEMS At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more. Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: Design, analyze, and perform trades studies to achieve programmatic targets.

You will have a focus in two areas: producing videos for our new Watch tab and producing video coverage on our live journalism team. This is a chance to be on the forefront of our newest initiatives and to participate in some of the biggest breaking news stories. You will be part of the first line of defense on developing stories, helping with innovating digital video news and doing ground-level reporting. You should have newsroom experience and a solid foundation of how to scout social platforms for video content, verify that content and identify video-storytelling opportunities. You should have a grasp of video production, from editing and shooting to scripting. You can work across breaking news, enterprise and investigations. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed. Responsibilities: Research and develop news stories for video, including sourcing relevant footage from social media, archives and news wires Help manage source material, and translation and transcription needs Verify the accuracy and authenticity of media reported across the web and social Contribute to video scripts and social copy

jobs.title: Fellow, Opinion Copy Editor
jobs.description_text: Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a copy editor for the Opinion section in New York. Copy editors are the last line of defense before publication of Opinion columnists, contributors and guest essayists. Basic duties include checking writers’ grammar, spelling and adherence to style and standards. An exceptional copy editor will also serve as an advocate for readers, ensuring that a story’s argument, logic, style and tone are sound. Opinion copy editors must balance enforcement of the standards of The Times with preserving a writer’s distinct viewpoint and voice. You have experience with copy editing and making editorial judgment calls. You can work collaboratively with story editors and fact-checkers. You are experienced digitally and enthusiastic about Opinion’s daily report — and open to working on stories from all points of view. You are platform agnostic and interested in working on copy for any medium. You are comfortable raising potential problems concerning standards and taste, and have good radar for when to push back on edits made by more senior colleagues. The Opinion department is separate from the newsroom. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed. jobs.title: Fellow, Photographer
jobs.description_text: Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a photographer. The Times is a worldwide leader in visual journalism, earning multiple Pulitzer Prizes and World Press Photo awards in recent years and establishing standards for excellence that have been influential across the industry. Our photographers bear witness to events around the world, and our Photo department is one of the treasures of our newsroom. As a fellow, you will work with Times photo editors, shooting daily news and enterprise assignments for many sections. The goal is to give you exposure to news and feature photography, and the opportunity to learn about news judgment, editing choices, video journalism, building visual narratives, lighting techniques and aesthetic direction. Working with photo editors, you will also initiate enterprise projects. You should be open to learning from others, and inclusive, generous and empathetic toward our colleagues, our audience, and the communities we cover. You will work out of either our New York headquarters, where you will cover a mix of assignments, or our Washington bureau, where you will mainly cover Capitol Hill and the White House. These are in-office positions and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. jobs.title: Fellow, Upshot
jobs.description_text: The Upshot is a small, versatile team that publishes analytical and explanatory journalism, often on policy and politics. And we often use data, visuals and interactivity to explain the world in new ways. As a fellow, you will pitch your own ideas and contribute to group projects in various forms. That work may mean visualizing the Caitlin Clark effect , showing political polarization in action , finding possible insider trading or tracking data centers from the sky . We are open to proposals on a range of roles. Typically, our fellows come with at least a year of reporting experience (or equivalent), along with technical or domain knowledge — in politics or policy, statistics or data analysis, information graphics, or web development. You don’t need to be an expert with data or technology, but you should be comfortable with it. And you don’t need to be a seasoned beat reporter, but you should be ready to pitch, report and write on complicated topics. Much of our best work involves working as a team. You should be excited about collaborating with other members of the Upshot and colleagues across the newsroom. Finally, we want you to know the Upshot and our work. Why do you want to work on this desk, as opposed to a different one? jobs.description_text: Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a Visual Investigations fellow in New York. The Visual Investigations team is looking for a digital sleuth with an innate curiosity and a journalistic urge to dig deeper. As a fellow, you will work with open-source reporters and video producers to break investigative stories and produce authoritative visual analysis on the biggest news of the day. You are proficient at doing digital research, mining social media and using the web to connect dots that reveal a bigger story. You can compile and assess visual content from satellite imagery, eyewitness videos and airplane- and ship-tracking platforms. You can also locate and verify user-generated content and be familiar with open-source reporting techniques. You will drive story ideas, be able to work autonomously and exercise sound news judgment. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. jobs.title: FOIA Editor
jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities. You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience. You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support. This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. We are curious about all kinds of things and seek to find individuals who bring their own curiosity to bear in creative approaches to storytelling. jobs.description_text: About the Role, Mission or Department Overview We are looking for a Research Lead with experience ensuring that shopping-centric insights are at the heart of product development. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that inform Wirecutter's strategy. Your projects will focus on helping connect our visitors to Wirecutter across the full shopping experience. Your research will inform audience strategy, content prioritization, and the Wirecutter Store, amongst other areas. You will be an important partner with Design, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data, Editorial, guiding decision-making and informing the teams' strategies. We at The New York Times seek the truth and help people understand the world. This mission is rooted in our belief that great journalism has the power to make each reader's life richer and more fulfilling, and all of society stronger and more just.
